paper.title: SKIP: Sparse Keyframe Interpolation Paradigm for Efficient Embodied World Models

claim: Efficient embodied world-model rollouts must preserve sparse task-relevant manipulation events such as approach, contact, grasp, and release; reducing inference cost by generic frame dropping can remove exactly the events downstream policies need.

evidence.summary: The paper argues that pixel-space rollout is expensive, but indiscriminate frame dropping is misaligned with embodied manipulation because critical task events may involve only small visual changes and become unrecoverable if omitted.
